name: Back Extension
summary: A posterior-chain exercise performed on an angled or horizontal bench to strengthen the lower back, glutes, and hamstrings.

setup: Position yourself face down in the back extension apparatus, anchoring the backs of your ankles securely under the rear pads.
Adjust the pelvic pad so that the top edge rests just below your hip crease, allowing your hips to fold freely.
Cross your arms over your chest or place fingertips lightly by your ears, maintaining a neutral spine and aligned neck.
steps: Hinge forward at the hips, lowering your torso in a controlled motion until you feel a deep stretch in your hamstrings.
Engage your glutes and hamstrings, driving your hips into the pad to raise your torso back up.
Lift until your body forms a straight line from your head to your ankles, pausing briefly at the top without hyperextending your lower back.
Lower under control to complete the rep.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you lower your torso toward the floor; exhale forcefully as you extend back up to the neutral finish position.
cues: Squeeze your glutes at the top

common_faults.fault: Hyperextending the lumbar spine at the top of the movement.
common_faults.correction: Finish the rep when your body forms a straight line from ankles to shoulders, relying on glute contraction rather than arching your lower back.

common_faults.fault: Setting the thigh pad too high above the hip crease.
common_faults.correction: Lower the support pad so it rests below the anterior superior iliac spine, permitting full hip flexion without restricting pelvis motion.

common_faults.fault: Using swinging momentum to propel the torso upward.
common_faults.correction: Perform both the eccentric lowering and concentric raising phases under smooth, deliberate muscle tension.

precautions: Ensure ankles are firmly secured under the rollers before hinging forward.
Individuals with acute lower back disc issues should maintain a strictly neutral lumbar spine and avoid loaded flexion.
